features.title: Fetch and snapshot Notion pages/blocks per workspace
features.user_visible_behavior: After connecting, the user's Notion pages and block snapshots are stored for the workspace.
verification: Trigger a sync for a connected workspace.
Verify Page rows exist for the workspace (notionPageId, tittle, workspaceId).
Verify Snapshot rows are created linking blockId, pageId, and userId.
evidence: Added the reusable sync routine server/lib/sync.ts: syncWorkspaceForUser(user) creates an authed Notion client from user.accessToken (auth-003), searches pages ({ property: 'object', value: 'page' }), upserts a Page per page on the stable notionPageId (tittle from the title-type property, fallback 'Untitled'; workspaceId from the user), then lists each page's top-level blocks and creates a Snapshot { blockId, pageId, userId } per block. Never logs the token; returns { pages, snapshots } counts.
The per-page upsert+snapshot block is wrapped in try/catch and continues on error so a duplicate `tittle` (Page.tittle is @unique) can't abort the whole run.

Added a thin trigger server/scripts/runSync.ts + server package.json script 'sync' (tsx --env-file=../.env scripts/runSync.ts). It resolves the first User with a non-null accessToken and calls the routine. The HTTP endpoint (sync-004 POST /sync) and 60s interval (sync-002) will reuse the same routine.
Baseline verified 2026-07-01: ./init.sh smoke check still PASSES (/auth/ -> 302, / -> 200); npx prisma generate OK. No schema change, no new dependency.
Live sync verified 2026-07-01: `npm run sync` against the connected workspace ddb7f940… (user id 1) printed 'Sync complete: 4 page(s) upserted, 86 snapshot(s) created' (token not logged).

DB assertions confirmed 2026-07-01: 4 Page rows with notionPageId, tittle ('Conflict Dasboard Flow', 'Accenture', 'Next js', 'Code Flow'), and workspaceId populated; 86 Snapshot rows linking blockId, pageId, and userId (all userId=1).
features.notes: Passing. Prisma models Page and Snapshot already existed; no migration. MVP limitations (deferred, not built): no pagination (first ~100 pages / ~100 blocks per page), no recursion into nested block children, no block content stored (Snapshot has no content column — conflict-001 owns adding it), single-user token drives a multi-user workspace sync. Snapshots are append-only (one row per block per run), giving sync-002 a time series.

features.title: Detect concurrent edits and record Conflict rows

verification: Create two snapshots for the same blockId by two different users.

Verify a Conflict row is created with pageId, blockId, user1Id, user2Id, and status='unresolved'.
evidence: Added server/lib/conflict.ts exporting detectConflicts(): groups all Snapshot rows by blockId, keeps each distinct userId's latest snapshot on that block, and for blocks with 2+ distinct contributors takes the two earliest-by-latest-touch as user1/user2. Dedupes against any existing Conflict for that blockId + user pair (either order) before creating, so re-runs don't spam duplicates. Creates with status='unresolved', resolvedBy='' (placeholder — Conflict.resolvedBy is non-null with no default; no migration needed).

Added server/scripts/runDetectConflicts.ts (thin trigger, mirrors runSync.ts) + server/package.json script 'detect-conflicts' (tsx --env-file=../.env scripts/runDetectConflicts.ts). A future sync-002 interval or endpoint can call detectConflicts() directly.

Verification status value changed from 'open' (as originally written here) to 'unresolved' to match conflict-003 (GET /conflicts filters status='unresolved'), conflict-004 (unresolved->resolved transition), conflict-005, and ALL_PHASE.md — 4 other entries vs. this one, and 'open' would have made detected conflicts invisible to the rest of the pipeline. Flagged for maintainer to confirm on review.
No schema change: the Conflict model already had every column needed (pageId, blockId, status, resolvedBy, user1Id, user2Id).

Verified 2026-07-02: DB had 1 User (id 1) and 129 Snapshot rows (all userId=1), 0 Conflict rows. Seeded a synthetic second User (id 6, email conflict-001-test-user2@example.com, same workspaceId as user 1) and one Snapshot (id 130) on an existing blockId ('3267f940-ff25-80ce-8952-fd1adad9c443')/pageId(1) with userId=6.

Ran `npm run detect-conflicts` (from server/): 'Conflict detection complete: 1 conflict(s) created.' DB query confirmed the row: pageId=1, blockId='3267f940-ff25-80ce-8952-fd1adad9c443', user1Id=1, user2Id=6, status='unresolved', resolvedBy=''.
Re-ran `npm run detect-conflicts`: 'Conflict detection complete: 0 conflict(s) created.' Conflict table count stayed at 1 row — dedup confirmed working.
Baseline: ./init.sh smoke check PASSES after the change (/auth/ -> 302, / -> 200). No schema/migration touched.

Cleanup 2026-07-02: deleted the seeded Conflict (id 1), Snapshot (id 130), and test User (id 6) rows after verification (in FK order) since the test user shared the real workspaceId and would have shown up as a real teammate/conflict in team-001/dash-002/dash-004 later. DB confirmed restored to the pre-verification state: 1 User, 129 Snapshot rows, 0 Conflict rows.
features.notes: Passing. Prisma model Conflict already existed (relations ConflictUser1/ConflictUser2). MVP limitations (deferred, not built): Snapshot.userId records who synced a block, not who edited it in Notion (no last_edited_by/last_edited_time captured), so detection is presence-based (2+ distinct syncing users on a block) rather than true concurrent-edit detection; no time window (any two contributors ever seen count, regardless of how far apart); with 3+ contributors on one block only the earliest pair is flagged (Conflict is a two-party model). The seed data used to verify this (test User id 6, Snapshot id 130, Conflict id 1) was deleted after verification rather than left in the DB, since the test user shared the real workspaceId and would otherwise appear as a real teammate/conflict in team-001/dash-002/dash-004. conflict-002/003/004 will need their own seeded Conflict row for their own verification.

features.title: 60-second polling snapshot engine
features.user_visible_behavior: Once a workspace is connected, its pages and block snapshots refresh automatically about every 60 seconds without any manual action.
verification: Start the server and connect a workspace so at least one Page row exists.
Confirm a setInterval (~60000ms) re-runs the sync-001 fetch+snapshot routine.
Wait for two intervals and verify new Snapshot rows (fresh createdAt) are appended for the same blocks.
Confirm the interval is set up once at server boot and does not stack duplicate timers on hot reload.
evidence: Added server/lib/syncScheduler.ts exporting startSyncPolling(intervalMs = 60_000) / stopSyncPolling(). Reuses syncWorkspaceForUser() (sync-001) unchanged. Selects the same 'first user with a non-null accessToken' as runSync.ts (prisma.user.findFirst), not all connected users — deliberate: conflict-001's detection is presence-based (2+ distinct syncing users on a block = Conflict), so auto-syncing every connected user every 60s would flood false conflicts the moment a second real user connects. Interval handle + an isRunning flag are cached on globalThis (same pattern as app/lib/prisma.ts) so a repeat startSyncPolling() call in the same process reuses the existing timer instead of stacking a new one, and an in-flight tick causes the next tick to log-and-skip rather than run concurrently. Token is never logged.

Wired into server/server.js: startSyncPolling() is called once inside the app.listen() callback (server boot); stopSyncPolling() added to the existing SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers alongside server.close().

Verified 2026-07-02: confirmed the stored connected user's Notion accessToken still works and measured real sync duration before designing the timing test — ran the existing 'npm run sync' (DB: 129 -> 215 snapshots, 4 pages, 86 new snapshots) and timed a second manual run at ~21s (mostly Notion API latency across 4 pages' worth of block-listing calls).

Exercised the scheduler live with a short interval via a throwaway script (not committed): called startSyncPolling(5000) twice back-to-back — logged 'Sync polling started: every 5000ms.' exactly once and the second call returned the identical handle ('Same handle returned: true'), confirming within-process idempotency. Note the scope of this check: server/server.js runs today via plain `tsx --env-file=../.env server.js` with no watch/dev mode, so this does not exercise a true hot-reload — the globalThis cache is the same mechanism that would protect a future `tsx watch` setup, matching the app/lib/prisma.ts precedent, but that scenario itself was not exercised.

Let the 5s-interval scheduler run ~50s against the real connected workspace: the live log showed several 'Sync poll complete: ... 4 page(s), 86 snapshot(s)' completions interleaved with 'Sync poll skipped: previous run still in progress.' lines — the overlap guard fired for real (each real sync run, ~21s, comfortably outlasts the 5s tick). The visible-log completion count was an undercount, corrected by a direct DB reconciliation (see next bullet); the properties actually being tested — ticks fire, overlaps get skipped, completions write real rows — are unaffected.

Reconciled exact run count directly from the DB rather than trust the captured log line count: total Snapshot rows went from 215 (after the token-check run) to 697 (net +482, real growth against the real workspace). Rather than back-compute a run count from the total delta (per-run size varies when a page is skipped, so that arithmetic doesn't reconcile cleanly), queried one specific blockId's own row history directly — unambiguous, since each run writes at most one row per block. That block shows 9 total rows: 2 pre-session (2026-07-01 and earlier 2026-07-02) plus exactly 7 new rows this session, timestamped 10:53:49 and 10:54:38 (the two manual runs: token-check + timing calibration) and five more between 10:55:22 and 10:56:01 (five real, non-skipped scheduler ticks during the ~50s live window) — one more completion than the live log appeared to show, confirming the scheduler ran (and the guard correctly let through) more real ticks than were visually counted from the terminal capture. Distinctness check: 86 distinct blockIds total (matches the workspace's real block count) — confirms genuine append-only time-series growth for the same blocks across every run, not new/different blocks appearing. These are real product snapshots against the real connected workspace, not synthetic test data, so they were intentionally left in the DB (not cleaned up, unlike conflict-001/conflict-002's synthetic seed rows).

Confirmed the production default without a live ~130s wait: started the real server (npm start --prefix server) and grepped its boot log for 'Sync polling started: every 60000ms.' — present. The tick logic itself was already proven live above on the same code path at a shorter interval, so this is a faithful substitute for waiting two full default-length intervals.

./init.sh baseline smoke check re-run after all verification: PASSES (/auth/ -> 302, / -> 200); npx tsc --noEmit (root) clean (server/ has no separate tsconfig / typecheck step in this repo's verification path, same as the existing server/lib/conflict.ts and server/lib/sync.ts). No leftover dev processes or listeners on 3000/3001 after verification; all throwaway test scripts deleted.
features.notes: Passing. Depends on sync-001 (passing). Design decision worth flagging on review: syncs only the first connected user per tick (matching runSync.ts), not all connected users — see evidence for the conflict-001 false-positive-flood reasoning; revisit once team-001/multi-user workspaces are real and conflict-001 detection gets a time window. detectConflicts() is deliberately not called from this interval (single_active_feature — that integration is conflict-001's note to a *future* feature, not this one). Token kept off logs throughout, per AGENTS.md.

Verify User, Page, Snapshot, and Conflict rows (mix of resolved/unresolved) are created.
Open http://localhost:3000/Dashboard and confirm the stat cards, chart, and lists render with the seeded data.
features.notes: Phase 7. Keep the seed idempotent/reset-safe so it can be re-run for demos.

features.title: Deploy to Supabase + Render + Vercel
features.user_visible_behavior: The app is reachable at a public URL: frontend on Vercel, backend on Render, database on Supabase.
verification: Provision the Postgres database on Supabase and run migrations against it.
Deploy the Express server to Render with the required env vars set (no secrets committed).
Deploy the Next.js frontend to Vercel pointed at the deployed backend.
Complete a live Notion OAuth login end to end and confirm the dashboard loads with real data.
features.notes: Phase 7. Update the Notion OAuth redirect_uri to the deployed callback URL. All secrets via platform env vars, never committed.
